description:
Plan: ../recursive-denotations-proposal.html. PR3 (fz-kdt.48), lands BEFORE fz-kdt.48.5. RE-SCOPED 2026-09-16 with the user's decision after the discharge was built and measured (see the comments; patch held as 48-10-discharge-NOT-LANDED.patch, not landed: +8 concepts, no census row moved on the settled seat, arm order still not free).

Measured on d25552951 and with the .48.5 patch (fz-wt-48g): at the boxed direct_call inside List.reduce_while_step/3's delivered_resume continuation, two arms A (take: s1 = {:cont | :halt, {[int], int}}, s2 = closure[Enum.take_positive]) and B (drop: s1 = {:cont, {[int], int}}, s2 = closure[Enum.drop_positive]) are Separated at the CLOSURE position (s2) and not at the tuple position (s1). The plan asks s1 before s2. So whichever separated arm is seated first, a value bound for the other arm answers the first arm's s1 (match), fails its s2, then answers its own s1 and s2: 3 matched questions instead of 2. The seat is an arbitrary canonical tie-break (order.rs lex_elements_then_longer clause count; .48.5's fusion flips it), which is why .48.5 moves SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP_CENSUS rows 9 -> 11 on 00418_enum_count_range and behavior/unused_range_binding while ten rows fall. Nothing on the path settles the covering s1, so no discharge can remove that question.

Build: within an arm, the plan asks the position(s) that SEPARATE it from its seated neighbours (the position where seating found no overlap) before the positions that do not, so a selection costs 2 questions in either seat by construction and separated-arm order becomes a pure determinism choice. Decide from seating's own per-position verdicts (typed containment on runtime tests), never from clause count or rendering; keep binding/projection edges where the arm below reads them. One rule, every producer (source patterns, callsite wrappers, construction wrappers), every door. Tests: the two-arm witness pinned at [2,2,2] matched questions for BOTH seats (the discharge builder's seating_the_covered_arm_first_is_what_shortens_the_walk_not_the_discharge test becomes this); the tie-break flip probe shows every SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP_CENSUS row unchanged under either seat; rows lowered in the same motion (expected: every row at or below 64 / 9 / 265 / 4, none raised); no golden rises; docs at canonically_order_separated_neighbours and order.rs say separated-arm order is determinism only, which is then a provable fact. Then .48.5 re-measures on top and must only lower rows.

comments.text: Built and measured 2026-09-16 on d25552951 (patch 48-10.patch held, not committed). Rule lives in dispatch_matrix (Proven carried down during construction; Proof::settles; resolved_target; relation = Types::covers = RuntimeTypePredicate::contained_in on the two TESTS, memoized as ComparisonKey::TestCovers, NOT is_subtype: the type->test projection is not monotone, e.g. {any,any} & not({:x,:x}) projects to a test admitting no tuple). Gate green (lib 2210/0, matrix 825/0). Findings: (1) the rebase onto main already moved SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP_CENSUS rows: 82->64, 12->9, 382->265 at d25552951; (2) on the settled seat the discharge moves NO row (the question it removes is a refuted one, never matched); plan node counts unchanged, only 4/2/4/2/2/0 miss edges retarget; (3) the ticket's neutrality claim is REFUTED: with the tie-break flipped, rows are 61/11/236 without the rule and 54/9/225 with it, still not equal to the settled 64/9/265 either way; cause = when the covering arm is seated first a value answers the covering question, fails the closure, then answers the covered question, and nothing on that path settles the covering question; (4) the patch is net +8 concepts (Proven, RegionCovers, Proof::settles, resolved_target, Types::covers, TestCovers, PatternResolver::covers, impl PatternResolver for Types) minus 2 no-op resolvers. The cure that makes arm order free by construction is asking the SEPARATING position first within an arm (dispatch_row precondition order): 2 questions in either seat. Also proposed, not filed: a dispatch graph holding only root-reachable nodes (61 unreachable fail nodes on json_roundtrip at baseline); one authority for test coverage (runtime_questions/seating re-project what Types::covers memoizes).

Framing (user, 2026-09-16): this is Maranget column selection. dispatch_matrix credits Maranget but compile_arm_sequence/compile_single_arm (mod.rs ~669-713) do no column selection: each arm is a chain of its own questions in the producer's order, misses fall to the next arm; the separating column (closure, input 2) is asked last only because it is input 2. Build as column selection in the tree compiler over the row block (necessity/separation from seating's containment verdicts on runtime tests, since our 'constructors' overlap), source order among ties; share a chosen column's test across the arms it separates if that collapses concepts. Not a per-arm reorder in the producer.

title: Ask the separating position first within a dispatch arm
